rationale: Iteration 10 (kd 0.2 to 0.3, everything else as iteration 8's best speed setting) is the best raced design at 56.8458, up from 46.1311. The gain came mainly from slalom progress rising from 0.036 to 0.111, with s-bend flat at 0.0415. The oval progress rose to 0.2734, but its line_loss_events rose from 1.7 to 2.2 and steering_oscillation from 0.17 to 0.16. The Evaluator's conditional rules were written against iteration 8. Rule (a) for keeping kd 0.3 and testing base_speed 1.6 needs oval line_loss at or below 1.7, which was not met. Rule (b) for reverting kd to 0.2 was written for a score of 46.13 and does not fit a result that beats it by 10.7 points. The final race is on unseen tracks and is scored once, so a measured design should beat an untested step. I therefore submit iteration 10's design unchanged: geometry outer sensors at +/-0.07 with inner sensors at +/-0.03 and 0, weights +/-1.5 and +/-0.75 with centre 0, base_speed 1.5, kp 2.5, ki 0.5, kd 0.3, last_direction. I do not test base_speed 1.6 here because the oval line-loss trend is already worse than the approval condition, and a speed step could cost more than it gains on an unseen track. Expected result, which is a reference rather than a prediction: a score near 56.8 on the development tracks. Watch whether the unseen track's line losses and off-track exits resemble the oval's pattern. Measurements requested: all metrics plus noise_robustness, so the result can be compared directly with iteration 10.
